title: The One-Way Street Out of Protein: Francis Crick's Central Dogma, Reverse Transcription, Prions, and the Myth of Molecular Heresy — Rescuing Francis Crick's real 1958/1970 Central Dogma from textbook 'DNA->RNA->Protein' caricatures; why Baltimore & Temin-Coffin retroviral reverse transcriptase, Fire & Mello's dsRNA interference & Chandramouly's 3.2-angstrom Pol-theta RNA-templated DNA repair sit cleanly inside permitted special transfers; testing Prusiner's nucleic-acid-free PrPSc prions, Shapiro's 21st-century genome-read-write challenge & Koonin's prion-to-genome assimilation; Shannon 10^127 codon-degeneracy entropy & UV target-size math plus reverse-ribosome falsification protocol

teenKit.tldr: High school textbooks lie: Francis Crick never said information flows in a rigid one-way line from DNA to RNA to protein. Real molecular biology allows complex nucleic acid transfers, meaning retroviruses and RNA repair fit safely inside Crick's original rules.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding the actual rules of genetic information saves us from sensationalized scientific myths and unlocks how modern gene therapy, retroviruses, and RNA-based medicines actually work.
keyTakeaways: The famous 'DNA to RNA to protein' linear arrow was actually drawn by James Watson, not Francis Crick, leading to decades of manufactured controversy.
Francis Crick's true Central Dogma was about sequence-information transfer: once information gets into a protein, it cannot flow back out into nucleic acids.
Discoveries like reverse transcriptase and RNA interference don't break Crick's dogma; they fit neatly into his original 1970 permitted transfers.

vocab.meaning: Francis Crick's rulebook governing how biological sequence information can and cannot move between DNA, RNA, and proteins.
An enzyme that defies the textbook caricature by copying RNA backwards into DNA, which is fully permitted under Crick's real framework.
Misfolded infectious proteins that spread disease by reshaping other proteins without needing a DNA or RNA instruction manual.
A cellular mechanism where small pieces of double-stranded RNA shut down specific gene expressions by targeting messenger RNA.

quiz.question: Who actually popularized the famous linear 'DNA -> RNA -> protein' cartoon in a 1965 textbook?
quiz.explanation: James D. Watson drew the simplified linear cartoon in his 1965 textbook, which later got misattributed to Francis Crick as an absolute dogma.

quiz.question: According to Francis Crick's actual 1970 diagram, which specific information transfer is strictly forbidden?
quiz.explanation: Crick's core restriction was that once information passed into a protein, it could never be reversed back into a nucleic acid sequence.

quiz.question: Why didn't the discovery of retroviruses overthrow Crick's Central Dogma?
options: Retroviruses transfer information from nucleic acid to nucleic acid (RNA to DNA), which Crick's 1970 model explicitly allowed.
Retroviruses use proteins to write directly into DNA, breaking all known biological laws.
Retroviruses do not carry any genetic information.
Crick changed his mind after retroviruses were found and abandoned the dogma entirely.
quiz.explanation: Crick's model forbade protein-to-nucleic-acid transfers, but nucleic acid-to-nucleic-acid transfers (like RNA making DNA) were entirely permitted in his original scheme.
